_: THE SWEEP THAT SAYS R1248's READER IS NOT VACUOUS — run it from the
repository root:
cargo run -q --manifest-path tools/injection-harness/Cargo.toml -- sweep \
tools/experiment-harness/injection-sweep.json
WHAT THE READER IS. A kit is a workspace validated by ONE revision, and
until R1248 nothing turned that declaration into the binary it names: thirty
of the thirty-two tracked kits declare a revision in their `replay.json`, no
kit `mnemosyne.toml` declares a `[tool] pin`, and the only code that could
materialise a revision lived in two `#[ignore]`d tests that each carried
their own copy.
SO THE FOUR INJECTIONS ARE THE FOUR WAYS IT ANSWERS CONFIDENTLY AND WRONG.
A kit that names two revisions gets the first. A record that never said why
it has no replay gets a word nobody wrote. A revision this clone does not
hold is reported as one that no longer builds, which is the sentence that
kills the pin design. And the cargo the caller named is quietly not the one
that ran, which is R1190 exactly. None of them fails to compile and none of
them prints an error.
RUN IT LOCALLY. The harness edits this tree and writes the firing record
beside this file, so a run sent to a build machine leaves its evidence on a
throwaway copy (R1205's carry, and the `writes` line in the declaration).

injections.name: a-kit-that-names-two-revisions-gets-the-first
injections.why: the confident wrong answer. Which revision reads a kit's artifact depends on which replay built it, and one kit really does name two — so collapsing the pair hands back a revision that arrives looking exactly like a right one, and the binary it builds refuses evidence for a reason that has nothing to do with the evidence

injections.name: a-record-that-never-said-why-answers-anyway
injections.why: an unfinished record and a decided one become the same record. `built-outside-this-repository` is an ANSWER — no revision of this repository ever ran that import — and a default word in its place says a person decided something nobody decided

injections.name: a-revision-this-clone-lacks-is-blamed-on-the-revision
injections.why: the two findings are not interchangeable and only one of them is alarming. A shallow checkout is the caller's problem and takes a minute to fix; `no longer builds` is the sentence that kills the pin-the-revision design for every replay that names it, and printing it about a revision that was never extracted would retire a kit for nothing

injections.name: the-listing-drops-the-kits-with-no-revision
injections.why: the quiet direction of an overview. Two tracked kits declare no replay and say why — one because no verb of this repository takes those bytes, one because an out-of-tree harness built them — and a listing that omits them reads as a tree where every kit has a revision, which is exactly the assumption this round exists to stop

injections.name: the-cargo-the-caller-named-is-not-the-one-that-runs
injections.why: R1190 at the seam where two tests now delegate. Both of them report a failed build as a finding about the REVISION and both pass their own toolchain in for exactly that reason; a build that silently used whatever PATH answers with would print that sentence about a channel difference, and the run would look identical
